2607.14651.title: MemPoison: Uncovering Persistent Memory Threats and Structural Blind Spots in LLM Agents
2607.14651.paper_summary: Persistent external memory enhances agent continuity but introduces persistent security vulnerabilities: adversarial content can be injected via standard interaction channels, retained across turns, and later distort downstream behavior. To address this challenge, we propose MemPoison, a comprehensive benchmark and analysis framework featuring 1227 hand-validated cases across four attack types, three injection channels, and three representative memory substrates, evaluated on seven open-weight and three closed-weight model families. We introduce a three-tier taxonomy: (L1) direct single-record corruption, (L2) compositional multi-record corruption and (L3) context-triggered dormant corruption. Our evaluations reveal a distinct defense frontier: while baseline write-time defenses, such as consistency checks, substantially suppress direct L1 attacks, they fail to reliably suppress L2 and L3 attacks. Through mechanistic influence decomposition (MID), we demonstrate structural blind spots in write-time defenses, which admit seemingly benign records that later become harmful through joint retrieval composition or trigger-conditioned activation. Our findings advocate for shifting from static filtering to adaptive, context-sensitive memory defense strategies.
2607.14651.paper_summary_zh: 持久的外部記憶增強了代理的連續性，但也引入了持久的安全漏洞：對抗性內容可以通過標準交互通道注入，並在回合間保留，隨後扭曲下游行為。為了解決這一挑戰，我們提出了MemPoison，一個全面的基準和分析框架，包含1227個經手動驗證的案例，涵蓋四種攻擊類型、三種注入通道和三種代表性記憶基質，並在七個開放權重和三個封閉權重模型系列上進行評估。我們引入了一個三級分類法：（L1）直接單記錄損壞，（L2）組合多記錄損壞和（L3）上下文觸發的潛伏損壞。我們的評估揭示了一個明顯的防禦邊界：雖然基線寫入時防禦，例如一致性檢查，顯著抑制直接的L1攻擊，但無法可靠地抑制L2和L3攻擊。通過機制影響分解（MID），我們展示了寫入時防禦中的結構盲點，這些盲點允許看似無害的記錄，隨後通過聯合檢索組合或觸發條件激活變得有害。我們的發現主張從靜態過濾轉向自適應的、上下文敏感的記憶防禦策略。
